architecture-review.json.boundary: No project, reference, store, registry, partial, module or provider dependency added. Existing Core journal owns atomic file/lease/CAS publication; planning owner owns decision transitions; the live capability delegates local invariant checks to the same owner. Cancellation transformation is reused from the existing saved-effect owner.
architecture-review.json.cycleReview: The owner/work pair now joins the existing journal/lease/claim type cycle because the actual saved dispatch lease carries the owner-issued work capability. This is one bounded in-process lifetime relationship within Core, not a project/module dependency or a new dispatch pipeline. The owner guard performs no IO and cannot mint a capability from persisted data. The other three existing local cycles are unchanged.
architecture-review.json.composition: Existing MAF saved dispatcher reaches the new work gate through the same journal claim path. Schema five retains its public admission; schema six requires the explicit planning-owner expectation and acknowledgement. Product activation and actual Workbench adapter remain subsequent work.
architecture-review.json.status: Pass with follow-up: bounded saved-action/lease integration only. Existing package advisories cause analyzer blocking status; no new diagnostic. Runtime tests, actual module integration and maximum-size/sustained capacity remain distinct gates.
architecture-review.json.repair: Only an undispatched schema-six prepared proposal with no dispatch claim or result can become a definite no-effect rejection. Schema-five decision semantics are unchanged. The actual Refresh regression exercises generation retirement and a new RunSnapshot/approval.

final-resource-reconciliation.json.outcome: 146 of 146 passed with observer active before both test lanes; reconciled before freeze release
